title: spike-interaction-phasefield-scratch-rory
content:
Objective:
Quick exploratory scratchpad to capture an odd spike interaction observed when interleaving low-QPS heavy-context requests with a background steady stream of short-chat queries. Trying to surface whether warm-KV-cache + adaptive batching + slot-slicing combinatorics produce a resonant slowdown ("phasefield" hypothesis).

Summary (TL;DR):
- Reproduced 3x p99 amplification at ~75s into a 10m run when 8 concurrent heavy requests (~8k tokens) are injected into a 200 QPS baseline of short requests.
- Amplification correlated with a transient KV cache eviction event on node hotpool; warmup priming overlapped with batching window boundary causing long tail.
- Short mitigation: reduce max-batch-wait from 8ms -> 4ms reduced p99 by ~40% but increased median CPU utilization by ~6%.

Experiment harness / config:
- Harness: local replay rig (wrk2-like synthetic driver) + request blender that issues two traffic classes: SHORT and HEAVY.
- Node: r5-gpu-4 (test fleet), runtime build: serving-runtime v1.18.0-rc (branch: phasefield-probe).
- Model: llama-2-13b-quant (kv-cache enabled).
- Baseline traffic: SHORT = 200 QPS, payload 16 tokens. HEAVY = 8 concurrent workers, 0.5 QPS each, payload ~8000 tokens (prefill heavy).
- Batching/settings toggled: max-batch-wait {2ms,4ms,8ms,16ms}, batch-size-cap {32,64,128}, kvcache-eviction-threshold {0.6,0.8}, prefill-parallelism {1,2,4}.

Key logs / observable sequence (timeline):
- 00:00 start: baseline SHORT steady at 200 QPS, p50=12ms, p95=28ms, p99=45ms.
- 01:20 HEAVY injection ramped up to target concurrency over 30s.
- 02:15 first noticeable p99 spike: p99 -> 150ms, p999 spikes to 420ms.
- 02:16 KV cache eviction event on node-hotpool-3 (evict triggered at 81% usage).
- 02:17 batching window collapsed: queued-heavy-prefill waiting for prefix -> long tail as heavy context fill serialized and blocked small requests at dispatcher due to slot-slice mutex.
- 02:50 system recovered; KV rewarm completed, tail decayed to baseline.

Quick numbers (selected runs):
- Run A (max-batch-wait=8ms, batch-cap=64, kv-threshold=0.8): p50=13ms, p95=36ms, p99=150ms, p999=420ms, CPU avg 62%, GPU util 48%
- Run B (max-batch-wait=4ms, batch-cap=64, kv-threshold=0.8): p50=15ms, p95=30ms, p99=90ms, p999=210ms, CPU avg 68%, GPU util 46%
- Run C (max-batch-wait=2ms, batch-cap=32, kv-threshold=0.6): p50=18ms, p95=42ms, p99=160ms, p999=480ms, CPU avg 72%, GPU util 40%

Interpretation / thoughts:
- Phasefield hypothesis: when heavy prefill requests overlap critical maintenance events (kv eviction, hotpool compaction) the dispatcher scheduling + batching heuristic falls into a pathological alignment where small requests get queued behind prefill operations, producing a resonant tail.
- Lowering batch wait reduces the window of accumulation and cuts the amplification, but tradeoff is higher CPU (more frequent smaller kernels) and slightly lower GPU amortization per token.
- Eviction threshold matters: lower threshold (0.6) caused earlier evictions -> more rewarm events and worse tails. But higher threshold keeps more cached entries at the cost of memory pressure — not always available for multi-tenant.

Quick ASCII chart (p99 over time, run A):
time(s)  0    30   60   90  120  150  180
p99(ms) 45   48   60  150  120   55   48

Notes on instrumentation gaps:
- Current trace sampling misses many of the short request traces during heavy prefill because sampling is token-count based. Need to bias sampling to short-event duration to see queue times.
- KV cache eviction log is coarse (1s buckets). For future runs enable per-eviction detail (may increase log volume).

Open experiments to run next (priority order):
1) Re-run with per-request trace sampling biased to <50ms events; capture dispatcher queue times.
2) Experiment with prefill-parallelism=1 vs 4 to measure serializer effect; hypothesis: fewer parallel prefill threads reduce mutex contention.
3) Try batch scheduling policy variation: prefer-small-requests flag (if available in runtime) -> route small requests earlier.
4) Introduce shadow traffic for non-critical routes to test degradations under real mixed tenant conditions.

Mitigations to try (quick):
- Short-term: set max-batch-wait=4ms for mixed-tenant clusters serving heavy prefills.
- Mid-term: add a soft lane for requests with small token count (prefer-small-requests) at dispatcher level.
- Long-term: make KV eviction incremental with background rewarm to avoid large eviction thrash during peak.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Capture a dump of hotpool slot mapping when next eviction happens (add ephemeral flag to runtime for debug).
- Add a tracepoint at dispatcher:time-in-queue and attach sampling to short requests.
- Write short PR to expose max-batch-wait override via per-tenant config.

References / useful links:
- local perf harness: /home/rory/dev/harness/run_blender.sh (use --blend-profile phasefield_v1)
- GH PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Linear task: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2112

End notes: this is a playground document. Keep lightweight; share to sofie/luca if next run reproduces consistently.
